fatal_errors: The proposed machine-learning-guided dealloying process replaces the target spray-drying/thermal decomposition-reduction method without supporting evidence.
The aqueous leaching conditions are incompatible with the target H2 reduction at 300°C and subsequent 400–500°C phase-tuning treatments.
The selective-leaching mechanism does not reconstruct the experimentally supported noble-metal-seeded, hydrogen-assisted reduction and solid-solution formation mechanism.
Neither cited source supports machine-learning optimization, dealloying of noble-metal HEAs, or production of the claimed three-dimensional nanoframeworks.
The hypothesis omits the key Pt/Ir/Ru versus Pd formation boundary, fcc/hcp phase control, methanol-oxidation conditions, and quantitative Pt-black comparison.
explanation: The response addresses the broad goal of producing porous NM-HEA frameworks and offers a potentially testable alternative, but it does not recover the reported method or formation mechanism. The target uses spray drying of homogeneously mixed salts followed by low-temperature H2 decomposition/reduction, where Pt, Ir, or Ru seeds hydrogen-assisted reduction and alloy incorporation. The generated account instead invents machine-learning-guided selective corrosion under liquid-phase acidic or alkaline conditions. Its generic predictions of increased surface area and catalytic activity only weakly overlap with the reported methanol-oxidation result. The proposed experiment can compare two dealloying optimization strategies, but it does not establish that dealloying is the relevant synthesis route and is weakened by unspecified post-processing. The cited papers provide only general HEA background and refractory-alloy additive manufacturing, so they do not validate the intervention or mechanism.
